findings.evidence: The ISSUE's Fix intent explicitly requires these behaviors. The inspected subject resolver, diff assembler and two BUILD writers are the corresponding consumers. The design addresses each, including the currently missing empty-subject guards. findings.premise: Empty subjects currently reach the judges, and the trivial implement route writes its initial BUILD record immediately after recording the build start.

These support both proposed amendments. findings.premise: resolveStoryRangeBase guarantees that a returned base resolves to a commit.
findings.evidence: Only the build-start stamp is checked with commitExists. stampedBase accepts 'typeof base === "string" && base.length > 0', and resolveStoryRangeBase then executes 'if (base !== undefined) return base'. An upstream artifact's stale or invalid meta.rangeBase is therefore returned without commit validation. The design's downstream Git-failure handling limits the impact, but its stated precondition is not guaranteed by this resolver. summary.prose: A Story's code review, its diff-only review and its BUILD records now decide the Story's files from the Story's own commits, the ones carrying its Insrc-Story trailer since its range base. An uncommitted change joins only when it edits a file those commits already changed; every other uncommitted change is left out and listed as excluded on the review record. With no range base to anchor on, the review declines instead of reviewing whatever the working tree holds. The build gate's typecheck project selection follows the same Story set.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Scope a Story's code review to what the Story changed, never a blind working-tree diff

api.name: changedFiles
api.signature: changedFiles(repoPath: string, opts?: ChangedFilesOptions): Promise<readonly string[]>

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: base (the Story's range base), storyKey (<epicHash>/<storyId>), exclude, excludeGlobs, onAttribution. With a base the Story's set is anchored on its commits; without one, today's working-tree derivation for callers that do not know a Story.

returns.meaning: With a base: the Story's set = the paths of its units (storyChangeSet with storyKey: trailer units, else every first-parent commit restricted to the Story's own paths), plus each working-tree path (unstaged or staged) that is already in that set; minus exclude. Every other working-tree path is reported, never returned. Without a base: unchanged (the working-tree derivation), for callers outside a Story.

errors.condition: git fails on the anchored derivation (as today).

opts.storyKey is given without a base: a Story's set has no anchor, so the seam refuses instead of returning the working tree (callers outside a Story pass neither and keep today's working-tree derivation).

preconditions: A base, when given, is a CANDIDATE commit (resolveStoryRangeBase checks only the build-start stamp with commitExists; an upstream artifact's meta.rangeBase is returned unchecked). One that does not resolve makes git fail, which is the NoBuildChangesError decline below, never a wider set.
postconditions: With a base, the result never contains a working-tree path outside the Story's committed set, whatever the working tree holds.
The order no longer depends on whether the tree is dirty: the Story's units are always read first.
onAttribution reports attribution ('story-trailer' | 'first-parent-range'), sharedWithExcluded and excludedUncommitted (the working-tree paths left out, sorted).
When opts.storyKey is given, storyChangeSet is called with strict: true, so a failed trailer scan fails the derivation instead of widening it to the first-parent range.

The anchored read selects per-unit diffs by set.perUnit, not by attribution === 'story-trailer': a filtered legacy range reads each kept unit's own diff, so a file another Story also edited (or later reverted) carries only this Story's change.

api.name: storyChangeSet
api.signature: storyChangeSet(repoPath: string, base: string, opts?: { readonly storyKey?: string | undefined; readonly strict?: boolean | undefined }): AttributedStoryChangeSet

parameters.name: opts.storyKey
parameters.purpose: <epicHash>/<storyId>: the trailer the Story's commits carry.

parameters.name: opts.strict
parameters.purpose: Anchored use (changedFiles with a storyKey, the diff-only grounding, the validate gate's selection): a trailer scan that cannot read the commit messages throws instead of falling back to the first-parent range. newestStoryCommit keeps the lenient scan.

returns.meaning: With commits carrying the Story's trailer: those units ('story-trailer'), as today. With a storyKey and NO commit carrying it: the first-parent commits that carry NO Insrc-Story line at all ('first-parent-range', the legacy pre-trailer Story); a commit carrying another Story's trailer is left out and its paths count as excluded (sharedWithExcluded). When every commit in the range belongs to another Story, the set is empty. Without a storyKey: unchanged. The result gains perUnit: boolean — true for 'story-trailer' and for a legacy range from which at least one other-Story commit was left out; false only for an unfiltered legacy range. FOREIGN COMMITS: the trailer scan records, besides the commits carrying the Story's trailer, the 'foreign' commits whose Insrc-Story lines all name other Stories. One rule then applies to every first-parent commit kind — an ordinary commit, a two-parent merge's merge-edit unit, and an octopus merge's whole-change unit: a foreign commit is never a unit (its paths are added to the excluded set and surface in sharedWithExcluded); a commit carrying the Story's trailer is a unit; an untrailered commit is a unit for a merge always (today's rule: merge edits are Story work unless they say otherwise) and, for an ordinary commit, only when no commit carries the Story's trailer (the legacy range). Leaving out a foreign commit makes perUnit true. PRE-TRAILER END (amendment 2026-10-21, after the t8 smoke on Epic c2ba6fa6 Story s1): in the legacy case (a storyKey and no commit carrying it), the range also ENDS at the Story's recorded build commit, resolveStoryRangeEnd: a first-parent commit after it is never a unit (it is later work, typically another person's untrailered commit such as 7d0e6402), its paths count as excluded, and perUnit is true. An end that does not resolve, or is not on the first-parent line of base..HEAD, is ignored with a warning (the legacy range runs to HEAD, as before). With a carrying commit the end is not consulted. An end EQUAL to the base is valid and means the Story has committed nothing attributable yet: the trivial implement route (src/daemon/steps/build-step/phases/implement.ts) persists the first BUILD record right after noting the build start, so its body.commit is the base. The legacy set is then empty (every first-parent commit since the base is after the end) and the review declines with 'no-build-record'. An end that is neither the base nor on the first-parent line of base..HEAD is ignored with a warning.

errors.condition: git fails on rev-list or a unit's diff (as today); with strict: true, also when the trailer scan cannot read the commit messages (today it logs and falls back).

postconditions: With a storyKey, the set never contains a unit from a commit carrying another Story's Insrc-Story trailer.
With strict: true, the attribution is never widened by a git failure.
perUnit is false exactly when the result equals today's unfiltered first-parent range, so the net-range read stays valid only there.

No unit of any kind (commit, merge-edit, octopus) comes from a foreign commit; untrailered merge edits are still kept, so today's 'only commits carrying the Story's trailer and merge edits are units' test is unchanged.
For a pre-trailer Story with a resolvable recorded end, no unit comes from a commit after that end, so an uncommitted edit of a file only a later commit touched is excluded, not joined.
The 'names this Story but lacks its trailer' warning fires only for an untrailered commit, never for a foreign one whose subject happens to read `<storyId>/`.

A recorded end equal to the base yields an empty legacy set, never the whole range; since a pre-trailer end never moves, an untrailered build begun on the trivial route is never attributed later untrailered work (the build prompt requires the trailer, which switches it to trailer attribution).

api.name: resolveStoryRangeEnd
api.signature: resolveStoryRangeEnd(repoPath: string, epicHash: string, storyId: string): string | undefined

returns.meaning: The full sha of the commit the Story's BUILD record names (body.commit: for a pre-trailer Story, HEAD when its record was last persisted), when it resolves to a commit; undefined when there is no record, no commit field, or it does not resolve. Read-only; never throws. Lives in src/workflow/runners/build/range-base.ts beside resolveStoryRangeBase.

postconditions: Used only by storyChangeSet's legacy case; a trailered Story never reads it.

The end is stable across every rewrite (validate reruns, completion, approval): persistBuildRecord computes body.commit as `rec.body.commit ?? storyCommit(...) ?? (prior.body.commit when it still resolves to a commit) ?? headShortSha(repoPath)` (an unresolvable prior value, such as a rewritten-away sha, falls back to HEAD as today), so once a pre-trailer Story's record names a commit it is never refreshed to a later HEAD. It advances only with evidence of new Story work: a commit carrying the Story's trailer, which also switches the Story to trailer attribution, where the end is not read. Checks, changeLog and the persisted record therefore all use the same end.

The existing case 'an explicitly SUPPLIED commit wins for that write; a later persist REFRESHES to HEAD' in src/workflow/runners/build/__tests__/build-record.test.ts is replaced: a later persist without a trailered commit KEEPS a prior commit that resolves, and refreshes to HEAD only when the prior one does not resolve.

api.name: storyRangeDiff
api.signature: storyRangeDiff(repoPath: string, base: string, set: StoryChangeSet & { readonly attribution?: StoryAttribution | undefined; readonly perUnit?: boolean | undefined }, excludeGlobs: readonly string[] | undefined, run?: (repoPath: string, input: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<DiffResult>): Promise<DiffResult>

parameters.name: set
parameters.purpose: The Story's change set; perUnit decides the read.

returns.meaning: With set.perUnit true, every path is read from the kept units' own diffs (today's 'story-trailer' branch: shared = set.paths); otherwise unchanged (net base..HEAD for plain paths, per-unit for sharedPaths).

postconditions: A filtered legacy range never grounds on another Story's hunks of a file both changed, nor loses this Story's change to a later revert by another Story.

api.name: resolveCodeReviewSubject
api.signature: resolveCodeReviewSubject(repoPath: string, epicHash: string, storyId: string, deps?: SubjectDeps): Promise<CodeReviewSubjectResult>

returns.meaning: The subject's changedFiles is the anchored set (base + storyKey + ledger exclusion); it carries changeSetAttribution, sharedWithExcluded and excludedFromScope (the working-tree paths left out).

errors.condition: No range base resolves for the Story, or git fails on the anchored derivation: the review declines; the two working-tree fallbacks are removed, so a failure never turns into a review of the working tree.

Amendment: the anchored set is EMPTY (the Story has no attributable change: a pre-trailer Story bounded to nothing, or a range of only other Stories' work). Nothing is reviewed and no record is written; today an empty set runs every judge and writes a vacuous pass record (src/workflow/code-review/runner.ts runs `for (const slot of judges)` unconditionally).

preconditions: The Story's build commits carry its Insrc-Story trailer (the tracked build's commit rule).
postconditions: changeSetAttribution is never 'working-tree' on a resolved subject.
The module header states the rule: the Story's commits decide its scope; the working tree only adds edits of its own files.

A resolved subject always has at least one changed file. The existing case 'resolveCodeReviewSubject: empty diff is a valid trivial subject (not an error)' in src/workflow/code-review/__tests__/subject.test.ts is replaced by the decline.

api.name: assembleDiffCodeReviewGrounding
api.signature: assembleDiffCodeReviewGrounding(repoPath: string, deps?: DiffGroundingDeps, opts?: DiffGroundingOptions): Promise<DiffGroundingResult>

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: base, excludeGlobs, storyKey, as the daemon RPC's degraded path and the controller step's diff-only path pass them.

returns.meaning: Per-file pseudo-symbols with hunks for the Story's set: its units' hunks, plus the working-tree hunks of files already in that set; changedFiles, changeSetAttribution, sharedWithExcluded and excludedFromScope.

errors.condition: No base was given, or git fails on the anchored derivation: the diff-only review is unavailable; the working-tree-first step and the last-commit step are removed.

preconditions: Callers pass the Story's base and storyKey (both callers already do).
postconditions: The diff-only review never grounds on a working-tree hunk of a file outside the Story's committed set, nor on another Story's last commit.

Amendment: both diff-only callers treat an empty changedFiles as the same 'nothing to review' outcome — src/daemon/code-review-rpc.ts ends the stream with an error whose reason is 'no-build-record', and src/daemon/steps/code-review-step/handler.ts returns errorResult('no-build-record', ...) — before any judge runs or any record is written. The assembler itself still returns an empty grounding (a valid value), so its own tests are unchanged.

api.name: collectBuildChangeLog
api.signature: collectBuildChangeLog(repoPath: string, ctx: { author: string; timestamp: string; version?: string; base?: string; exclude?: readonly string[]; storyKey?: string }, listChanged?: (repoPath: string, opts?: ChangedFilesOptions) => Promise<readonly string[]>): Promise<ChangeLog>

parameters.name: ctx.storyKey
parameters.purpose: <epicHash>/<storyId>, forwarded so the BUILD record's changeLog follows the same anchored rule (trailer units).

returns.meaning: The BUILD record's file-level changeLog of the Story's set; unchanged swallow of a git failure to [].

postconditions: The completion record and the validate phase pass the Story's storyKey, so an unrelated uncommitted file never enters a BUILD record's changeLog.

With ctx.storyKey and no ctx.base (resolveStoryRangeBase returned undefined), the seam refuses (NoBuildChangesError) and the swallow yields an empty changeLog: a Story's BUILD record never falls back to the working tree.

Both writers (completion-record.ts and validate.ts) write changeLog whenever they pass a storyKey, even when it is empty, instead of omitting an empty one: mergeWithPrior's { ...prior.body, ...rec.body } then replaces a prior changeLog (including one contaminated by the old working-tree derivation) rather than keeping it. The md renderer already omits the ## Changes section for an empty changeLog.

Change site (amendment): src/workflow/runners/build/standalone-record.ts persistBuildRecord prefers the prior record's body.commit over HEAD when the Story has no trailered commit; neither writer changes.

api.name: withTypecheckProjects
api.signature: withTypecheckProjects(repoPath: string, plan: ValidationCheckPlan, base?: string, storyKey?: string): ValidationCheckPlan

parameters.name: plan
parameters.purpose: The gate's plan; plan.testFiles still always contribute their projects.

parameters.name: storyKey
parameters.purpose: <epicHash>/<storyId>; src/daemon/steps/build-step/phases/validate.ts passes it at its one call, inside the shared runValidateSession that both the plan-driven and the standalone routes enter. The trivial route's own selection is trivialCheckPlan, which validate.ts also calls with the key.

returns.meaning: Stays synchronous. With a storyKey, the private changedFiles helper lists the Story's set synchronously: storyChangeSet(repoPath, base, { storyKey, strict: true }).paths plus the uncommitted and untracked paths already in that set; with a storyKey and no base, no changed files (only plan.testFiles' projects). A listing that fails is logged and contributes nothing, as today. Without a storyKey: today's three listings.

postconditions: With a storyKey, a project that owns only unrelated uncommitted or untracked files is not added to typecheckProjects.
The projects of plan.testFiles are always included, whatever the change set.

api.name: trivialCheckPlan
api.signature: trivialCheckPlan(repoPath: string, base?: string | undefined, storyKey?: string | undefined): ValidationCheckPlan

returns.meaning: With a storyKey and a base, the test files are those in the Story's set (storyChangeSet with strict: true) that still exist in the checkout, instead of every file in base..HEAD (the existence filter keeps today's --diff-filter=d rule: a deleted test, or one added then removed, is never asked to run); with a storyKey and no base, the listing fails as 'no range base' (listError), failing the tests check rather than running the HEAD commit's tests. Without a storyKey: unchanged.

postconditions: A trivial build never runs another Story's tests as its own.
A test file the Story deleted is never in the plan.

api.name: splitDiffByFile

parameters.name: body
parameters.purpose: A unified-diff body, possibly the concatenation of several git diff outputs (unstaged, staged, per-unit).

returns.meaning: Per new (b/) path, every section for that path in body order, joined with a newline; a later section is appended, never replacing an earlier one (today map.set keeps only the last). Header paths are decoded the way git writes them: an unquoted `diff --git a/<old> b/<new>` line, or a quoted one, `diff --git "a/<old>" "b/<new>"`, which git uses for a path with a tab, newline, double quote, backslash or (with core.quotePath) a non-ASCII byte; the quoted form's C escapes (\t, \n, \", \\ and octal \nnn bytes, decoded as UTF-8) are undone, so the section is keyed by the literal new path that git_diff's -z numstat reports.

postconditions: A file with both staged and unstaged edits keeps both sets of hunks in the diff-only grounding.

Every file git_diff lists has its hunks found by its literal path, including a renamed file and a path git quotes, so no Story file falls back to `[no hunk text for ...]` while the diff body is complete. When git_diff's body cap (256 KB by default) truncates the body, a file past the cap may still carry no hunk text; the grounding is then marked `[diff truncated — reviewed over a bounded slice]`, as today, and that limit stands.

api.name: realDiffGroundingDeps().workingTreeDiff
api.signature: workingTreeDiff(repoPath: string, excludeGlobs?: readonly string[]): Promise<DiffResult>

returns.meaning: The union of the unstaged and staged diffs: per path, the file stats are summed (insertions and deletions of both), not overwritten by the staged entry; the body keeps both sections, which the accumulating splitDiffByFile then keeps per file. The anchored grounding keeps only the paths in the Story's set.

errors.condition: Either git diff read fails (runDiff rejects), as today.

postconditions: No staged or unstaged hunk of a Story file is lost or double-counted when the two are combined with the Story's committed hunks. (within an untruncated body; see splitDiffByFile)

api.name: runShell
api.signature: runShell(argv: readonly string[], options?: ShellOptions): Promise<ShellResult>

returns.meaning: Amendment (cycle 3 round 2): stdout and stderr are decoded with a node:string_decoder StringDecoder per stream (decoder.write per chunk, decoder.end at close) instead of `chunk.toString('utf8')`, so a multibyte UTF-8 character split across two chunks is decoded whole. Byte accounting for maxBytes and stdoutTruncated is unchanged; a chunk past the cap is still dropped, and the decoder is ended so a partial character at the cut is not emitted as replacement text silently past the truncation flag.

postconditions: A path containing multibyte characters reaches git_diff's parser exactly as git wrote it, so Story membership and hunk lookup agree for it. src/daemon/tools/shell-helper.ts is the change site; every runShell caller benefits unchanged.

api.name: gitDiffTool.execute

parameters.name: input
parameters.purpose: As today (cwd, from/to, staged, paths, exclusions).

returns.meaning: When the numstat command exits non-zero (the body command succeeded), the result is success: false with error naming the numstat failure, instead of success: true with an empty file list. Its consumers (changed-files.ts collectDiff and grounding.ts runDiff) already reject an unsuccessful result, so a failed stat read becomes NoBuildChangesError / DiffUnavailableError and the review declines. RENAME-SAFE PATHS (amendment, review round 3): the numstat command runs with -z, and the parser reads its NUL-delimited records: `<ins>\t<del>\t<path>\0` for a file, and `<ins>\t<del>\t\0<old path>\0<new path>\0` for a rename or copy. path is the literal new path and origPath the literal old path, never git's compact display form `dir/{a => b}/file` (which the current parser at src/daemon/tools/builtins/git/diff.ts:311 splits into `b}/file`). Paths with spaces, tabs or ` => ` in them are read literally too. CAPTURE LIMITS (amendment, cycle 3 round 1): runShell drops a whole chunk once output passes its cap and reports stdoutTruncated (src/daemon/tools/shell-helper.ts:90-115), so (a) GitDiffData.truncated is `diff.stdoutTruncated || diff.stdout.length >= maxBytes` (today it reads only the captured length, so a dropped chunk below the cap goes unmarked), and (b) a numstat read with stat.stdoutTruncated, or whose NUL-delimited records end mid-record, returns success: false naming the incomplete file list, which collectDiff and runDiff already turn into NoBuildChangesError / DiffUnavailableError.

errors.condition: git cannot be spawned, the diff body command fails (as today), or the numstat command fails (new).
The numstat output was truncated by the capture cap, or its NUL-delimited records are incomplete: the file inventory cannot be trusted.

postconditions: An apparently empty file list from git_diff always means git reported no changed file, never a failed read.

Every path git_diff reports is a real repository path, so membership checks against storyChangeSet's paths (diff-tree names) and the per-file hunk lookup by the body's `b/` path agree for renamed files.
A body that lost output is always marked truncated, and a file list that lost output is never returned as complete.

dataModelChanges.details: excludedUncommitted: readonly string[] — the working-tree paths the anchored derivation left out because no Story commit touched them (sorted). Empty when none.
excludedFromScope?: readonly string[] — the uncommitted paths left out of this review; absent when none, so a clean tree's subject is unchanged.

excludedFromScope?: readonly string[] stamped on the review record next to changedFiles, changeSetAttribution and sharedWithExcluded, so a reader sees what was left out and why; absent when none (existing records stay valid).
A resolved subject's attribution is 'story-trailer' or 'first-parent-range'; 'working-tree' stays in the type for records written before this fix but is never produced for a Story's review.

errorCases.scenario: No range base resolves for the Story (no BUILD start stamp, no resolvable commit).
errorCases.detection: resolveStoryRangeBase returns undefined in resolveCodeReviewSubject (and the diff-only callers pass no base).
errorCases.response: The review declines with today's reason 'no-build-record' (the diff-only path raises DiffUnavailableError); nothing is reviewed and no record is written. It never falls back to the working tree.
errorCases.userImpact: The reviewer is told the Story has no anchored change set, instead of receiving a review of someone else's edits.

errorCases.scenario: git fails on the anchored derivation (rev-list, trailer scan or a unit's diff).
errorCases.detection: storyChangeSet or collectDiff throws NoBuildChangesError (DiffUnavailableError on the diff-only path).
errorCases.response: The subject declines with 'no-build-record' (the diff-only review is unavailable); the step-down to a plain working-tree derivation is removed. A BUILD changeLog still swallows the failure to [] as today.
errorCases.userImpact: A broken git state ends the review clearly rather than silently reviewing the tree.

errorCases.scenario: The working tree holds uncommitted changes outside the Story's committed set (another person's work, another Story's in-progress edits).
errorCases.detection: The working-tree diff is read after the Story's units; each path not in the Story's set is set aside.
errorCases.response: Left out of changedFiles and the grounding; reported on the subject and the review record as excludedFromScope (sorted); logged once per review with the count.
errorCases.userImpact: The review judges only the Story; the reader sees exactly which uncommitted files were left out.

errorCases.scenario: The trailer scan cannot read the commit messages (git log fails) on an anchored derivation.
errorCases.detection: storyChangeSet's scanTrailers throws instead of returning undefined, because the anchored callers pass strict: true.
errorCases.response: NoBuildChangesError: the review declines with 'no-build-record' (DiffUnavailableError on the diff-only path), the BUILD changeLog is empty, and the gate's typecheck selection adds no changed-file projects. The derivation never widens to the first-parent range on a failure.
errorCases.userImpact: A git failure cannot turn into a review of other Stories' commits.

errorCases.scenario: A Story's BUILD record is written but no range base resolves for the Story.
errorCases.detection: resolveStoryRangeBase returns undefined in completion-record.ts or validate.ts; collectBuildChangeLog is called with storyKey and no base.
errorCases.response: changedFiles refuses (NoBuildChangesError) and collectBuildChangeLog swallows it to []: the record carries no changeLog rather than the working tree's files.
errorCases.userImpact: The BUILD record says nothing about files rather than claiming unrelated ones.

errorCases.scenario: The git_diff builtin's diff body command succeeds but its numstat command fails.
errorCases.response: The tool returns success: false; collectDiff throws NoBuildChangesError and runDiff rejects, so the review declines with 'no-build-record' (DiffUnavailableError on the diff-only path) and a BUILD changeLog is empty.
errorCases.userImpact: A partial git failure can no longer pass as 'the Story changed nothing'.

errorCases.scenario: The Story's anchored change set is empty.
errorCases.detection: resolveCodeReviewSubject's changedFiles, or the diff-only grounding's changedFiles, has no entry.
errorCases.response: Decline with 'no-build-record' (the diff-only callers end with that reason); no judge runs and no record is written.
errorCases.userImpact: A Story with nothing attributable gets no vacuous pass verdict.

errorCases.scenario: git_diff's numstat output is cut by the capture cap (very many files) or ends mid-record.
errorCases.detection: stat.stdoutTruncated, or the last NUL-delimited record is incomplete.
errorCases.response: git_diff returns success: false; the anchored derivation declines ('no-build-record' / DiffUnavailableError) instead of reviewing a partial file list.
errorCases.userImpact: A huge change cannot silently lose files from its review.

invariantsToPreserve.text: A clean tree's change set is byte-for-byte today's committed-range result for a range with trailer units, and for a legacy range in which no commit carries another Story's trailer. A legacy range holding another Story's trailered commits changes deliberately: those commits are left out (the existing story-commits-trailer.test.ts expectation of ['src/a.ts', 'src/b.ts'] for a Story with no carrying commit becomes ['src/a.ts']). Likewise a range holding a merge whose message carries only another Story's trailer changes deliberately: that merge's edit (or octopus change) is left out. A range with no foreign commit of any kind is unchanged. Also changed deliberately: a legacy range shortened by the Story's recorded build commit (a pre-trailer Story with a BUILD record whose commit is before HEAD) leaves out the commits after it, on a clean tree too; the existing clean legacy tests have no BUILD record and are unchanged.
The only decline reason of resolveCodeReviewSubject stays 'no-build-record'; CodeReviewSubjectResult's shape is unchanged.
LEDGER_EXCLUDE_GLOBS and the caller's exclude list still apply to every diff the derivation runs.
collectBuildChangeLog never fails a build: a git failure is still swallowed to [].
Existing review records stay valid: the new excludedFromScope field is optional and absent when nothing was excluded.
A trailered Story's set never depends on its BUILD record; the recorded end is read only when no commit carries the Story's trailer.

migration.stateBefore: changedFiles returns the whole working-tree diff as the Story's change set whenever the tree is dirty, and reads the Story's trailered commits only on a clean tree (src/workflow/runners/build/changed-files.ts:142-178, c1). The review subject steps down from the anchored derivation to two working-tree-only derivations on a git failure (src/workflow/code-review/subject.ts:150-213, c2); the diff-only grounding reads the working tree first and, with no base, the last commit (src/workflow/code-review/grounding.ts:282-320, c3). The BUILD record writers call collectBuildChangeLog without a storyKey, and the validate gate lists typecheck projects from base..HEAD plus every uncommitted and untracked file (c4). On 2026-10-21 this reviewed six unrelated ontology files as Epic c2ba6fa6 Story s1 (ISSUE-b97752e9c7cee6fe). Build progress at this amendment (2026-10-21): migration steps for the shared seam, review subject, diff-only grounding, record field, BUILD writers and validate gate are built (plan tasks t1-t7, commits 873c4c3e..a0a031cf); the pre-trailer range end, the stable recorded end and rename-safe git_diff paths are the remaining work, followed by the installed-daemon smoke.
migration.stateAfter: With a Story's base, changedFiles always anchors on the Story's commits (trailer units, else its first-parent own paths) and adds only working-tree edits of files in that set; every other uncommitted path is reported (excludedUncommitted) and, on a review, stamped on the subject and the record as excludedFromScope. The review subject and the diff-only grounding have no working-tree or last-commit fallback: without a base, or when git fails, they decline. The BUILD records pass the Story's storyKey, and the validate gate selects typecheck projects from the same Story set. A clean tree's results are unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Change the shared seam's order for callers that pass a base: anchor on the Story's units, then add working-tree paths already in the set, and report the rest; add excludedUncommitted to the attribution report. storyChangeSet gains strict and, with a storyKey but no carrying commit, leaves out commits carrying another Story's trailer; changedFiles refuses a storyKey without a base. It also returns perUnit, which changedFiles uses to choose per-unit diffs. The trailer scan also records foreign commits, and the foreign rule applies to merge-edit and octopus units too.

Add resolveStoryRangeEnd and end a pre-trailer Story's legacy range at its recorded build commit inside storyChangeSet; restrict the missing-trailer warning to untrailered commits. persistBuildRecord keeps a prior body.commit instead of refreshing it to HEAD when the Story has no trailered commit, so the end never moves for a pre-trailer Story.

Read git_diff's numstat with -z so a renamed file is reported by its literal paths. splitDiffByFile decodes git's quoted diff headers so hunks are keyed by the same literal paths. git_diff marks the body truncated from the shell's stdoutTruncated flag and fails a truncated or incomplete numstat read. runShell decodes output with a StringDecoder so multibyte paths survive chunk boundaries.
Remove the review subject's two working-tree fallbacks, carry excludedFromScope on the subject, and update its module header to the new rule.

Apply the same rule in the diff-only grounding (Story units plus own-file working-tree hunks; no working-tree-first or last-commit step) and in both diff-only callers. storyRangeDiff selects per-unit reads by set.perUnit. splitDiffByFile accumulates every section per file and workingTreeDiff sums staged and unstaged stats.
Stamp excludedFromScope on the review record (optional field, absent when none).

Pass the Story's storyKey from the BUILD completion writer and the validate phase (an unresolved base then yields an empty changeLog), and pass it to withTypecheckProjects and trivialCheckPlan (both stay synchronous, through storyChangeSet with strict) at both validate.ts call sites. Both writers write the changeLog even when empty, so a re-write replaces a contaminated prior one; trivialCheckPlan keeps only Story test files that still exist.
Make the git_diff builtin fail (success: false) when its numstat command fails.

Decline an empty anchored set with 'no-build-record' in resolveCodeReviewSubject and both diff-only callers; replace the 'empty diff is a valid trivial subject' and 'later persist REFRESHES to HEAD' expectations.

Update the tests (including validation-checks.test.ts's uncommitted/untracked expectations, now only without a storyKey) that asserted working-tree-first scoping; rebuild and update the installed daemon; re-run the observed case (a review with unrelated uncommitted files) on it.

migration.backwardCompat: No IPC payload or public signature changes: changedFiles, resolveCodeReviewSubject, assembleDiffCodeReviewGrounding and collectBuildChangeLog keep their signatures (one optional ctx field, storyKey, is added to collectBuildChangeLog). New record fields (excludedFromScope, excludedUncommitted) are optional and absent when nothing is excluded, so existing records validate. 'working-tree' stays in the ChangeSetAttribution type so older records still parse. Behaviour change by design: a review that used to judge a dirty tree now judges the Story's commits and lists the rest; a review with no resolvable base now declines. Deliberate behaviour change for legacy ranges containing other Stories' trailered commits; the affected trailer-test expectation is updated. git_diff now reports a failed numstat read as a failure; every consumer already handles success: false. Amendment: a pre-trailer Story's legacy range now ends at its recorded build commit, so later untrailered commits leave its set; trailered Stories are unaffected.

alternativesConsidered.name: The Story's commits decide the scope; uncommitted changes join only through its own files
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Derive the Story's set from its trailer-scoped commits first; add an uncommitted change only when it touches a file in that set; report every other uncommitted path as excluded; no blind fallback.
alternativesConsidered.approach: One rule in the shared seam (changedFiles), used by every caller that knows the Story. With a base and a storyKey, the Story's set is its trailer-scoped units (storyChangeSet), exactly as today's clean-tree path computes it; the working-tree diff is then read and split: a changed path already in the Story's set is added (an in-progress edit of the Story's own file), every other path is excluded and reported through onAttribution as excludedUncommitted. The attribution says 'story-trailer' (or 'first-parent-range' when no commit carries the trailer). Without a resolvable base the Story has no committed work to anchor on: the review declines rather than reviewing the tree. The code-review subject drops its two working-tree fallbacks (a git failure on the anchored derivation declines with today's 'no-build-record'), carries excludedFromScope on the subject and the record, and its header states the new rule. The diff-only grounding applies the same rule to its hunks (Story units, plus uncommitted hunks of the Story's own files) and loses its working-tree-first and last-commit steps. The BUILD record collectors pass the storyKey so their changeLog follows the same rule.
pros: Exactly the approved fix intent: the Story's own change set is the authority and unattributable changes are reported, never judged.
Reuses what exists: storyChangeSet, the trailer, resolveStoryRangeBase, onAttribution; one rule in one seam, so the review, the diff-only path and the BUILD records cannot disagree.
An in-progress edit to a file the Story already changed is still reviewed.
cons: A Story whose work is entirely uncommitted (no trailered commit yet) has nothing to review; the tracked build commits before validate and review, so this matches the workflow, but an ad-hoc review before the first commit declines.
Changes asserted behaviour in the existing attribution tests, which must be updated.

alternativesConsidered.name: Attribute uncommitted files also by the Story's own records
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: As a1, but an uncommitted file also counts as the Story's when its PLAN tasks or BUILD record name it, so pre-commit work can be reviewed.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Everything in a1, plus a second attribution source for uncommitted paths: the files the approved PLAN's tasks or the BUILD record's changeLog name. An uncommitted path is the Story's when its commits touched it OR its records name it; everything else is excluded and reported. This lets a review run before the Story's first commit, provided its records name the files.
pros: Reviews pre-commit work that the Story's records anticipate.
Still excludes unrelated changes by default.
cons: Records name files loosely (PLAN task summaries are prose, BUILD changeLogs are themselves derived from this seam), so attribution becomes fuzzy and circular: the BUILD record's changeLog would partly attribute itself.
More machinery than the fix intent asks for; adds a flexibility nobody requested.

alternativesConsidered.name: Refuse to review a dirty tree
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep today's derivation, but when the working tree has any uncommitted change outside the ledger, decline the review and list the dirty paths.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The subject resolver and the diff-only path check the working tree first; any non-ledger uncommitted path makes the review decline with a new reason naming the paths. A clean tree reviews the Story's trailer-scoped range as today.
pros: Smallest change; never reviews an unrelated file.
cons: Blocks every review while anyone edits anything in the repository (the 2026-10-21 case: someone else's ontology work would stop this Story's review), which is the opposite of excluding unrelated changes from the scope.
Drops the Story's own in-progress edits instead of attributing them; the BUILD records still absorb unrelated files.
